decision: RECEIPT-ONLY NEGATIVE: land no source change. Giving each lane two or four output rows (R independent accumulators, R concurrent weight-row streams, one shared x load) is bit-identical to the shipped kernel as designed and verified, but it LOSES decisively on the M1: +29.4/+29.6 percent us/layer at R=2 and +46.2/+52.8 percent at R=4 in the in-model widedep instrument, both legs, far past the -3 percent win bar in the wrong direction. The last untested memory-level-parallelism structure for the Q4 decode GEMV is now measured-dead; the 41 GB/s vs 60 GB/s roof gap is not per-lane-MLP-recoverable within the pinned arithmetic order. Nothing merged; branch rows-per-lane (5bcae341) carries the bench arms, raw legs and this receipt only.
question: Does raising per-lane memory-level parallelism by giving each lane 2 or 4 output rows (two or four independent accumulators issuing concurrent load streams from different weight rows, x loads shared) move the Q4 decode GEMV toward its 60 GB/s layout roof, bit-preserving, and win by >=3 percent repeatably?
arm_design: Slot (32 lanes) covers R consecutive output columns instead of one; lane j walks the SAME words it walked for each column in the shipped kernel (w = j, j+32, ...; the qmv_fast tile preserved as dead code for K%512==0), each dot/input_sum chain and per-word block finish keep the shipped sequence, and the 32-lane reduction keeps the shipped stride-1-first pairing per column (interleaved scratch columns in tree mode). Only the workgroup->column map changes: grid shrinks by R (COLUMNS_PER_WG = 8*R). x is loaded once per w-step and shared across the R rows; each step issues R weight-word loads from rows words_per_row*4 bytes apart before any arithmetic.

what_limits_it: The kernel's 41 GB/s is 69 percent of its own layout roof, but the deficit is not a per-lane MLP deficit: rows-per-lane multiplies per-lane live state (35 -> 63 -> 87 gprs) and the straight-line instruction stream (600 -> 1132 -> 2066 instrs) while total weight bytes per layer are fixed, so achieved bandwidth FALLS (41.0 -> 31.6 -> 27-28 GB/s). max_threads stays 1024 across all arms, so the occupancy table does not cap threads; the cost is register liveness and issue overhead, the same class as the prefetch-depth ladder from receipts/2026-09-11-q4-memory-roof. Latency was already hidden by thread-level parallelism; the remaining gap to the roof lives elsewhere (reduction/barrier structure and CDM issue), consistent with that receipt's conclusion. The R-way weight streams also do not help the real limiter: with one lane per row-walk, each stream is one word per lane per step, and widening the streams was measured (wider uvec4, 2.7 percent pattern-level only) without surviving at model level.
observed_not_landed: wg128 showed -4.25/-4.42 percent vs base in both of today's gap legs (196.7/196.8 vs 205.4/205.9 us), but receipts/2026-09-11-q4-memory-roof measured it bimodal across windows (+0.34/-4.43) and owns that verdict; recorded here as context only, ownership stays there.
